scenes.title: 1976 Surrey AV Suite: Sliding a White Paddle Across the TV Screen Flips 'DA-DA' Into 'BA-BA'
scenes.era: 1976, University of Surrey Audiovisual Psychology Suite, Guildford, UK

layout.description: Sunlit 1976 British university audiovisual control desk holding a wood-trimmed studio television monitor showing open-mouth 'GA' lip articulation, an unobstructed desktop loudspeaker cone beside an unchanged 'BA' waveform meter, and a rigid white cardstock occlusion paddle.

positions.who: Harry McGurk (2.5D matte cream-white vinyl psychologist in 1976 British tweed blazer and patterned tie)
positions.where: standing beside the wood-cabinet TV monitor sliding a white cardstock paddle directly in front of the screen without touching the loudspeaker

positions.who: John MacDonald & 40-year-old adult listener (2.5D matte cream-white vinyl figures in collared shirts and knitwear)
positions.where: seated across the control desk leaning toward the speaker and flipping between bold 'DA' and 'BA' response cards in disbelief

props.name: sliding white cardstock screen-occlusion paddle
props.period_detail: handheld opaque board covering ONLY the television lips while leaving the desktop speaker cone 100% unobstructed
props.physical_behavior: State-A held aside exposing screen (listener holds up 'DA' card) -> State-B slid smoothly across the TV glass (listener instantly swaps to 'BA' card)

props.name: 1976 wood-trimmed studio monitor paired with desktop loudspeaker cone
props.period_detail: stages the exact Surrey dubbing room split between visual 'GA' lips and pure 'BA' sound waves
props.physical_behavior: State-A synchronized audiovisual playback -> State-B unchanged speaker cone vibrating steadily while screen is blocked

actions.verb_sequence: plays repeating loudspeaker track with TV uncovered -> slides white paddle squarely across the TV face without touching audio dial -> pulls paddle away again
taps 'DA' card confidently with eyes on screen -> gasps and taps 'BA' the instant the white paddle blocks the lips

reactions.reaction: astonished laugh covering and uncovering their own eyes to test the instant DA-to-BA flip
wry grin logging 98% adult phantom fusion on the 1976 Surrey tally sheet

scenes.wardrobe: 1976 British university attire: warm brown tweed jacket, wide-collar shirt, striped tie; adult volunteer in navy V-neck jumper.
scenes.lighting: Clean high-key 1976 British studio window daylight.
scenes.recognition_hook: Nobody touches the speaker volume or audio tape — just slide a white card in front of the TV screen and 'DA-DA' flips instantly into 'BA-BA'!

key_visual.description: a 1976 British audiovisual lab desk where a researcher slides a white paddle across a wood-trimmed TV monitor beside a desktop loudspeaker while a seated adult flips between DA and BA cards

scenes.title: Sunlit Outdoor Sidewalk Cafe Terrace: Putting On Glasses Unlocks Effortless Conversation Over Street Buzz
scenes.era: Modern sunlit outdoor sidewalk cafe patio

layout.description: Vibrant open-air neighborhood sidewalk cafe terrace under morning sun where two 50-year-old spouses sit across a bistro table; putting on eyeglasses and turning into clear sunlight turns muffled street-side chatter into crystal-clear speech.

positions.who: 50-year-old adult diner (2.5D matte cream-white vinyl figure in linen blazer)
positions.where: putting on clean tortoise-shell glasses at the outdoor bistro table and leaning forward in bright sunlight
turning chair into the warm morning sun so lip movements are clearly visible while speaking

props.name: tortoise-shell eyeglasses and espresso cups on sunlit outdoor bistro table
props.period_detail: captures the relatable midlife 'I can hear you better with my glasses on!' phenomenon
props.physical_behavior: State-A folded beside espresso saucer (diner squinting and cupping ear) -> State-B unfolded onto face as shoulders relax in instant comprehension

actions.verb_sequence: lifts eyeglasses from bistro table and slips them on -> faces speaking partner in open sunlight -> nods and laughs catching every word cleanly

reactions.reaction: warm, effortless connection once 100-ms visual lip cues prime auditory cortex

scenes.wardrobe: Adult weekend smart-casual wear: light navy linen blazer, crisp white shirt, tortoise-shell frames.
scenes.lighting: Bright natural morning sunlight across open sidewalk cafe awning and greenery.
scenes.recognition_hook: Putting on your glasses at a bustling outdoor cafe genuinely helps you HEAR — because your temporal lobe lip-reads every consonant a tenth of a second early!

scenes.title: 2012 Neuroimaging & Attention Suite: Temporal-Lobe Mixing Board Weighting Sight + Sound

layout.description: Clean sunlit cognitive neuroscience suite where an adult listener wears studio headphones facing a high-speed lip-sync display beside a 3D superior temporal sulcus brain diagram.

positions.where: tracking 100-ms visual lip lead feeding into the temporal lobe mixing hub

props.name: studio headphones and audiovisual timing waveform board
props.period_detail: illustrates visual lip motion leading vocal audio by ~100 ms into left STS
props.physical_behavior: State-A unaligned tracks -> State-B locked audiovisual fusion wave

actions.verb_sequence: aligns lip-motion curve ahead of audio wave -> highlights strong STS fusion response

reactions.reaction: fascinated nod seeing how eyes prime ears automatically

scenes.wardrobe: Clean white lab coat and smart-casual sweater.
scenes.recognition_hook: Human lips shape a consonant 100 milliseconds before vocal cords buzz — giving your temporal lobe a built-in sneak preview.
